sonnet.problem: The answer is already given by earlier cards. Card 1 says Saul put the troops under an oath, card 2 asks what the oath forbids, and cards 3 and 5 say no soldier tastes food or touches the honey. Card 6 then asks why they won't touch the honey, and "They feared the oath" is the same fact again.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. Once a choice has been answered, the cards after it can build on that answer. An easy follow-up is fine. ... An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: The card tells Saul's plan of violence ("leaving no man alive") and also carries a cookie joke.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: The summary card for the family list goes item by item. It names the three sons, two daughters, wife, Abner, Ner, Kish and Abiel, when it should say in a few words what the stretch covers.
sonnet.rule: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick.
